Coronavirus infections predominantly involve respiratory tract mucosa; other organ damage is not common across this umbrella.
Inflammatory disease of retinal blood vessels; ocular location, vascular injury and immune/infectious mechanism define it.
Intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; myopia/amblyopia and pituitary hypothyroidism each reported in 1/1; very small series limits certainty.
Multiple dermal sebaceous cysts define disease; kidney stones are occasional (5–29%) and separately diagnosed.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy directly affects red cells and spleen; listed chest, brain and bone complications lack evidence of common qualifying damage.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; macular degeneration is frequent (30–79%). Oculomotor signs are neurologic; pes cavus alone does not establish tissue damage.
Hereditary susceptibility to ovarian cancer; reproductive organs have no axis, and susceptibility alone does not establish organ damage.
Inherited retinal cone dysfunction/dystrophy causing achromatopsia.
Skeletal dysplasia; microtia 2/2, cardiac defects 1/1 and vesicoureteral reflux 1/1 support additional axes; small denominators limit certainty.
Labial adhesion affects external reproductive anatomy; no specific urinary tract disease is established.
Recessive skeletal dysplasia involving cranial and clavicular development; no supported additional organ involvement.
Usher type I is defined by sensorineural hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal dystrophy.
Fragile X syndrome subtype; inherited neurodevelopmental impairment defines the organ axis.
Severe bladder voiding dysfunction defines syndrome; reflux and hydronephrosis share the renal axis. Constipation alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Encapsulated thymic epithelial tumor; thymus has no listed anatomical axis. Thymoma alone does not establish immune dysfunction or lymphoma.
Syndrome defined by skeletal enchondromatosis with dwarfism and hearing loss; no additional organ evidence supplied.
Skeletal anomalies and impaired intellectual development define the syndrome umbrella.
Disordered cortical recognition of fingers; this is neurologic dysfunction rather than disease of the fingers themselves.
Stippled cartilage and skeletal dysplasia define umbrella; ichthyosis and intellectual disability vary substantially by subtype and are not established across most patients.
Benign mature teratoma arising in the stomach.
Carotid arterial aneurysm; stroke is a separately diagnosed complication. Cranial nerve paralysis is occasional (5–29%); broader nerve findings do not establish lasting damage.
Bone fragility, osteopenia and congenital joint contractures define Bruck syndrome; collagen-processing defect alone does not add a metabolic axis.
Structural myocardial disease causing ventricular dysfunction and conduction abnormalities; thromboembolic complications are occasional.
Stromal tumor originating in the colon or rectum; aggressive behavior alone does not establish another organ axis.
